::: {.block title="Methods"}
We trained a separate model for each 10 m depth bin from the surface to 200 m to predict $\log_{10}(\mathrm{Chl}\,a)$ from $R_{rs}$ (11 or 172 bands), local solar hour, and sampling platform. We tried several model types (boosted regression trees, multilayer perceptrons, XGBoost); results here use boosted regression trees (BRT), which train quickly. Local solar hour allowed the model to account for daytime quenching of in situ chlorophyll fluorescence. Each profile was matched to the nearest grid cell in the same-day Level-3 $R_{rs}$ map. We evaluated out-of-sample skill using five repeats of grouped fivefold cross-validation, keeping all profiles within each 1° × 30-day block in the same fold. We report $R^2$ of $\log_{10}(\mathrm{Chl}\,a)$ per depth bin and of integrated Chl *a*: Chl *a* summed over the 10 m bins from the surface to 200 m or the deepest observed bin (profiles reaching at least 50 m).
:::
